note: Curated list (team decision 14.11 23:45). Each event is described only as far as its sources describe it. The box is an approximate area for matching, drawn around the region the sources name; the match window adds a short tolerance for monthly data. expected_direction is given only where the source states the direction of the change for that variable; otherwise the direction is not checked. A match means 'consistent with', never 'caused by'.

events.title: Breach of the Kakhovka dam, Ukraine

dates.as_described: The dam was breached on 6 June 2023; the reservoir emptied and the canals fed by it dried up in the following weeks.

area.description: Former Kakhovka reservoir on the Dnipro and the river downstream to Kherson (approximate box).

sources.title: Canals in Ukraine are Drying Up

dates.as_described: Cataclysmic eruption on 15 June 1991; the sulfur dioxide spread around the planet lowered global temperatures by about 0.5 °C for roughly 1991 to 1993.

area.description: The cooling described by the source was global.

sources.title: The Cataclysmic 1991 Eruption of Mount Pinatubo, Philippines (Fact Sheet 113-97)

events.title: Drop in nitrogen dioxide during the COVID-19 lockdown, northern Italy

dates.as_described: Satellite data from 1 January to 11 March 2020 show nitrogen dioxide over Italy falling, most clearly over the Po Valley, which ESA links to the lockdown.

sources.title: Coronavirus: nitrogen dioxide emissions drop over Italy

events.title: Drop in nitrogen dioxide during the COVID-19 shutdown, China

dates.as_described: NO2 over China was much lower on 10-25 February 2020 than on 1-20 January 2020; about three months later the levels had returned to near normal.

area.description: Central and eastern China shown in the NASA images (approximate box).

sources.title: Airborne Nitrogen Dioxide Plummets Over China
Nitrogen Dioxide Levels Rebound in China

events.title: Drop in nitrogen dioxide during the COVID-19 lockdown, northeastern United States

dates.as_described: OMI on NASA's Aura satellite measured March 2020 NO2 over the northeastern U.S. about 30 % below the March 2015-2019 average, the lowest March in the OMI record.

area.description: Northeastern U.S. from Washington, D.C. to Boston (approximate box).

sources.title: NASA Satellite Data Show 30 Percent Drop in Air Pollution Over Northeast U.S.

dates.as_described: MODIS daytime land surface temperatures in July 2003 were up to about 10 °C higher than in July 2001 over southern and eastern France; the heat wave was responsible for at least 3,000 deaths in France.

area.description: France, where the source shows the strongest heating (approximate box).

dates.as_described: MODIS land surface temperatures for 20-27 July 2010 were far above the 2000-2008 average over western Russia, while part of northern central Russia was below average.

events.title: Heat and drought in northern and central Europe, 2018

dates.as_described: Summer 2018 was the warmest on record for Europe; northern and central Europe had a prolonged drought, with less than 80 % of normal precipitation in spring, summer and autumn in the most affected regions.

sources.title: European State of the Climate 2018 launched

dates.as_described: A wide and persistent lack of precipitation combined with heatwaves from May 2022; by early August 47 % of Europe was under drought warning and 17 % under alert, worsening in northern Italy, south-eastern France, Hungary and Romania.

area.description: Western, central and southern Europe (approximate box).

sources.title: Drought in Europe - August 2022 (GDO Analytical Report, JRC130493)
Summer drought keeps its grip on Europe

events.title: Floods in western Germany and Belgium, July 2021

dates.as_described: Record rainfall on 14 July 2021 (ERA5 daily mean of 92.6 mm over a region on the Belgium-Germany border) caused floods on 14-15 July; river discharge in parts of the Meuse and Rhine basins was the highest since 1991. Copernicus EMS mapped the flooding in western Germany (activation EMSR517).

area.description: Eifel region of western Germany and eastern Belgium (approximate box).

sources.title: EMSR517: Flood in Western Germany (Rapid Mapping activation)
European State of the Climate 2021: Flooding in July
